**Why join us?

**Muuto is rooted in the Scandinavian design tradition characterized by enduring aesthetics, functionality, craftsmanship and an honest expression. By expanding this heritage with forward-looking materials, techniques and bold creative thinking, our ambition is to deliver new perspectives on Scandinavian design.

We are looking for a commercially minded and analytical Category Manager to strengthen our global supplier network, drive category performance, and support the continued growth of our business.

As Category Manager, you will play a key role in developing and managing supplier relationships, improving operational performance, and ensuring that our supply chain remains scalable, resilient, and aligned with Muuto’s ambitious growth plans.

**Key Responsibilities

**You will be responsible for a portfolio of suppliers and product categories, working closely with Product Development, Sustainability, and Commercial teams.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Developing and executing category strategies aligned with business objectives

• Managing supplier relationships, negotiations, and performance reviews

• Driving continuous improvements in lead time, delivery performance, quality, and cost

• Identifying and implementing sourcing opportunities and risk mitigation plans

• Leading supplier development initiatives and supporting dual sourcing strategies

• Monitoring KPIs and using data-driven insights to improve category performance

• Supporting new product introductions from design to market launch

• Collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders to optimize supply chain performance

• Ensuring supplier compliance with Muuto standards, sustainability requirements, and business processes

• Driving transparency and reporting across supplier and category performance

**WHO ARE YOU?

**We imagine that you have:

• A bachelor’s or master’s degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business, Procurement, or a related field

• 5+ years of experience within Category Management, Procurement, Strategic Sourcing, or Supply Chain

• Strong negotiation and stakeholder management skills

• Experience managing international suppliers and complex supply chains

• Strong analytical capabilities and experience working with KPIs and performance management

• Commercial understanding combined with a collaborative and relationship-focused approach

• The ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution

• Excellent communication skills in English

• Experience from furniture, design, consumer goods, or manufacturing industries will be considered an advantage.

**WE OFFER

**At Muuto, you become part of an international design company where creativity, collaboration, and entrepreneurship are part of everyday life.

You will get:

• A key role in shaping supplier and category strategies

• Exposure to a global supplier network

• Close collaboration with design, product development, and commercial teams

• Opportunities for professional and personal development

• A dynamic, informal, and ambitious work environment

• The chance to contribute to one of the strongest design brands in the Scandinavian industry

You will report to the Supply Chain Manager, and the position is expected to start as soon as possible.

To learn more about Muuto, our products, and our designers, please visit Muuto.com.

If you are interested, please upload your CV and application via the link as soon as possible.

**At Muuto, our mission is to deliver new perspectives on Scandinavian design. We are an international team of ambitious and passionate people - all driven by the desire to expand on the Scandinavian design tradition with a forward-looking, creative and honest approach. We are looking for qualified applicants representing a wide range of backgrounds and abilities who share this same mindset. Individuals who wish to actively contribute and bring their opinion to the table. Individuals who would like to bring a wealth of new perspectives to our company.

That is why we are always keen to hear from talented people who wish to join our company - regardless of gender identity, age, sexual orientation, ethnicity, racial identity, religious belief and disability status. We are committed to equal opportunity employment.

To learn more about Muuto, our products and designers, please visit www.muuto.com

jobs.occupation: Senior Hardware Productization Engineer / Mechatronics Lead
jobs.description:
The role

We are looking for a senior hardware/product development engineer with strong experience taking physical products from prototype through engineering validation and into manufacturing.

You will work directly with the founder and take ownership of the physical architecture of Dreamspire.

This is not primarily a firmware role and it is not a pure industrial-design role.

We need someone who can look at a prototype and systematically turn it into a product.

You should be comfortable moving between:

• mechanical engineering

• electronics integration

• manufacturing

• prototyping

• reliability

• assembly

• suppliers

• cost

• compliance

• user experience

A large part of the work will initially be hands-on.

Your first mission

Your first objective will be to create a clear Dreamspire Product Architecture V1.

You will examine the existing prototype, identify its weaknesses and determine how we should build the next generation of the system.

This includes answering questions such as:

• Which prototype mechanisms are suitable for a real product?

• What needs to be redesigned?

• Which components should be custom versus off-the-shelf?

• How should cameras, lighting, electronics and mechanical systems be integrated?

• How do we make assembly simple and repeatable?

• What are the major reliability risks?

• What manufacturing processes should we use?

• What should the production BOM look like?

• What needs tooling?

• What can initially be produced in low volume?

• What compliance and certification work will be required?

• How do we move from one prototype to 10, 100 and eventually thousands of units?

The objective is not to rush into manufacturing.

The objective is to progressively remove technical and manufacturing risk until the product is ready.

Responsibilities

You will:

• Audit the existing Dreamspire hardware and mechanical architecture.

• Design and build improved prototype generations.

• Own mechanical design and product engineering.

• Integrate cameras, PCBs, lighting, power, cabling, connectors and sensors into the physical product.

• Design enclosures, mounts, mechanisms and structural components.

• Define tolerances and mechanical interfaces.

• Design for manufacturing and assembly — DFM/DFA.

• Reduce part count, assembly complexity and manufacturing cost.

• Select appropriate materials and production methods.

• Decide when to use CNC, sheet metal, 3D printing, injection molding or other processes.

• Work with PCB/electronics engineers where specialist electrical work is required.

• Develop production BOMs and cost estimates.

• Source and evaluate components and suppliers.

• Communicate directly with prototype houses and manufacturers.

• Design test fixtures and production test procedures.

• Establish reliability and lifecycle testing.

• Help define EVT, DVT and PVT stages.

• Identify CE, EMC, electrical safety and other relevant compliance requirements.

• Help design the system for serviceability and repair.

• Help prepare Dreamspire for small pilot production and eventually mass production.

What we are looking for

The most important requirement is:

You have personally helped ship real physical products.

Ideally, you have taken products through several stages of:

prototype → engineering validation → manufacturing → production → customer

You should have strong practical experience with several of the following:

• Mechanical engineering

• Mechatronics

• Consumer electronics

• Product development

• DFM / DFA

• CAD

• Injection-molded plastic parts

• CNC and rapid prototyping

• Electronics packaging

• PCB integration

• Cameras / optical systems

• Sensors

• Motors or electromechanical systems

• Tolerance analysis

• Supplier management

• BOM optimization

• Production testing

• Reliability testing

• Manufacturing ramp-up

You should be comfortable physically building, modifying and debugging prototypes rather than only designing them.

Particularly relevant backgrounds

Experience from products such as these would be especially relevant:

• Consumer electronics

• Robotics

• Smart-home products

• Interactive toys

• Gaming hardware

• IoT products

• Camera systems

• Medical or laboratory devices

• Small electromechanical products

Experience working in a startup or small product-development team is a major advantage.

What we are not looking for

This is probably not the right role if your experience is primarily:

• Arduino hobby projects

• Pure firmware development

• PCB design without product/mechanical ownership

• Industrial design without engineering responsibility

• CAD work without manufacturing experience

• Large-company engineering where manufacturing and suppliers were handled entirely by other teams

We are looking for someone who understands the whole physical product.

How you work

You should enjoy environments where the product is still evolving.

You should be able to say:

“This prototype mechanism works, but it will not survive production.”

or:

“We can remove these five components if we redesign this assembly.”

or:

“Don’t spend money tooling this yet — we need to validate this part first.”

We want someone who challenges assumptions and prevents expensive mistakes rather than simply implementing specifications.

Working with the founder

You will work closely with the founder, who currently develops the software, computer-vision systems, embedded systems and game concepts.

You will therefore have considerable influence over the architecture of the product.

The expectation is that you become the technical owner of the physical Dreamspire platform, while working closely with software and game development.

If the collaboration works well, the role could evolve into something resembling:

Head of Hardware / Head of Product Engineering

as Dreamspire grows.

Location

The role is based around Copenhagen.

Much of the work can be done remotely, but during prototype development we expect regular hands-on work with the physical Dreamspire system.

Candidates elsewhere in Denmark or the Øresund region are welcome if they can work regularly in Copenhagen.

Employment

We are open to:

• Full-time employment

• 3–4 days/week

• An initial senior consulting/fractional arrangement that can develop into a permanent role

For a strong permanent candidate, expected salary is approximately:

65,000–75,000 DKK/month + pension, depending on experience.

Exceptional candidates with significant consumer-product leadership experience may be above this range.

Why this role is interesting

Dreamspire is not another incremental electronics product.

The aim is to create an entirely new category of tabletop gaming platform and then build multiple games on top of it.

The fundamental question is:

Can we create something with the physical presence and social experience of a board game, but with systems and mechanics that were previously only practical in video games?

A large part of whether that succeeds depends on making the hardware disappear into the experience.

That is the problem we want you to help solve.

How to apply

Email jobs@dreamspire.dk with your CV and a few lines about the physical products you have helped ship. We read every application and use it only to assess it; see how we handle your data.

ROLE ACOUSTIC ENGINEER

TEAM PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT

**

• You'll select and design acoustic components based on product and market requirements.

• You'll define initial enclosure concepts.

• You'll build and evaluate proof-of-concept prototypes to validate acoustic concepts.

• You'll collaborate with Mechanical Engineering during the early product development phase to mature acoustic concepts.

**

• You'll validate simulation results through physical testing.

• You'll collaborate with suppliers to refine acoustic components based on simulation and test results.

• You'll own the technical specification of loudspeaker drivers towards suppliers.

• You'll define driver specifications and tolerances.

• You'll support manufacturing verification with suppliers.

• You'll participate in the acoustic verification of the final product towards mass production.

• You'll collaborate with the Audio team on audio signal handling, including crossovers, compressors, and limiters.

• You hold a BSc or higher in Audio, Acoustics, Mechanical, or a related engineering discipline.

• You've done loudspeaker simulation and measurements, and use both to validate and refine your designs.

• You've worked with loudspeaker development from concept through verification and ideally have experience collaborating with external manufacturing partners.

• Familiarity with crossover design, FEM simulations, or failure analysis is an advantage.

• Ideally you also have experience building physical speaker mock-ups or collaborating with large-scale loudspeaker manufacturing partners.

• You work independently, take ownership of your area, and enjoy collaborating closely with engineers across disciplines.

• You're curious, creative, and constantly looking for ways to improve acoustic performance.

• You're drawn to what SOUNDBOKS is building and are excited to be a part of the journey!

Intrigued? At SOUNDBOKS you’ll find yourself a part of a community. We realize that growth is a process and we don’t expect you to go through it alone. Actually, we guarantee that you won’t have to. We work together in order to work smarter, we inspire each other to be better, and we never forget that every member of the team is responsible for our success.

So, if you’re tired of all of the noise in the job market, we’d love to hear from you. This may be the coolest job you ever have!

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Reality Capture for Digital Twinning of Built Structures - DTU Compute
jobs.description:
The aim of this project is to develop technologies for creating building information models of existing built structures. This is part of a larger goal of using digital techniques to support sustainability in construction - specifically by making it easier to repurpose buildings.

Responsibilities
You will work within the area of visual computing. Much of the work will be based on machine learning and in particular vision language models. The use of generative methods will be central to your research whose overarching goal is to study how it is possible to extract information about a construction from photographs and other data sources and generate a precise building information model with little or no user input.

You will be affiliated with CEBE (Civil Engineering and the green transition in the Built Environment) which is a Danish cross-university research programme focusing on the sustainable development of the built environment. CEBE’s vision is to promote science-based circular, low-carbon and resilient built environment within planetary boundaries. CEBE is supported by the Villum Foundation.

You will be matriculated at the DTU Compute PhD School, employed at DTU Compute, and embedded in the Section for Visual Computing. The Section for Visual Computing is focused on medical image analysis, geometry and appearance modelling, computer vision, multivariate statistics for images and analysis of 3D microstructures. Within these areas, our overarching research aim is to make methodological contributions of broad applicability but motivated by applications.

Qualifications
To qualify for this position, you must have a background in visual computing (computer graphics and computer vision), a good understanding of the basics of computer-aided design and machine learning. These qualifications must be underpinned by a strong background in applied mathematics. 

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

At DTU Compute, we have a large focus on creating a good working environment. Our work with diversity and inclusion is an essential part of that. We believe that having a good working environment is a necessary foundation to provide excellent research, teaching, supervision and innovation.

At DTU Compute, we have about 140 PhD students. We offer several events and activities for all our PhD students such as annual PhD Bazaar, onboarding course where you will meet other PhD students, and you can join our PhD Club that organizes BBQs, board games events, lunches etc. 

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is 1 February 2027 or according to mutual agreement. The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Andreas Bærentzen, janba@dtu.dk. 

You can read more about DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU.

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. jobs.description:
If you want to design the electronic properties of a material rather than simply measure them, this PhD puts the tools in your hands. When two-dimensional crystals are stacked with a controlled twist, or when a periodic pattern is imprinted into them, an artificial superlattice emerges in which the band structure can be reshaped and bandgaps opened by design, using a novel combination of 2D materials and freestanding oxide membranes. 

You will create such materials yourself in a group that has worked with 2D materials for two decades and with full access to the cleanroom and microscopy infrastructure at DTU Nanolab. The project is part of METRIQS and is carried out together with national and international partners.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall focus will be to create and control superlattices in graphene and other 2D materials, and to establish how the engineered structure translates into an engineered electronic band structure. You will pursue two complementary routes: assembling hybrid van der Waals heterostructures in which the moiré periodicity is set by twist angle and lattice mismatch and imprinting periodic patterns directly into the 2D material or its supporting layers by nanofabrication. Both routes call for careful design, reproducible processing and close comparison between intended and realised structure. You will work with colleagues at DTU Physics and DTU Nanolab and with partners in the METRIQS collaboration. 

Your primary tasks will be to:

• Design superlattice geometries and device layouts, using modelling and simulation to decide what is worth fabricating.
• Assemble hybrid van der Waals heterostructures from graphene, hBN, transition metal dichalcogenides and related materials with controlled twist and alignment, using a newly developed semi-automatic stacking system, and collect data on stacking recipes and results to obtain and document optimal parameters through datamining and statistics. 
• Imprint periodic patterns into 2D materials and their supporting layers using electron beam lithography, etching, thin film deposition and related nanofabrication.
• Fabricate devices in which the engineered materials can be contacted, gated and measured.
• Characterise structure and electronic properties by scanning probe microscopies, electron microscopies, Raman spectroscopy, optical spectroscopy and electrical transport at cryogenic temperatures. 
• Connect the measured electronic response back to the intended superlattice design, and iterate on the design.
• Establish reproducible fabrication and measurement protocols, analyse your data and present the results in publications and at conferences.
We are looking for a candidate with a background in physics, nanotechnology, materials science, electrical engineering or a related field. You should have hands-on experience with micro- or nanofabrication or comparable experimental laboratory work, and be comfortable with systematic work, data analysis and programming for design, automation or modelling. Experience with 2D materials, layout and CAD design, electron microscopy or electronic transport is an advantage, but the project spans several techniques, and we do not expect you to bring all of them with you. We value curiosity, persistence and the ambition to take ownership of your own project.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.
